scope: A v3.4 sticky-open target component with exact unique common-core state, complete target-component failed-bucket coverage, and pairwise-disjoint residual scopes after conditioning on that state.

theorem.statement: Within the frozen scope, the conditioned target conjunction is exactly representable as an additive portfolio of independently projected residual boundary factors. The factor-local payload Cartesian product need not be materialized. The transformed boundary problem may be handed to the already sealed guarded-elimination engine, and any admitted transformed witness can be reconstructed and replayed against every original relation.
theorem.unique_core_requirement: |S| = 1 where S is the exact common-core support intersection inherited from v3.4.
theorem.complete_coverage_requirement: The failed-bucket factors are exactly all relations of the target cut component.
theorem.residual_independence_requirement: After removing the common core C, residual scopes are pairwise disjoint.
theorem.portfolio_rule: Condition on the unique s, existentially project factor-local private residual variables to each local boundary scope, retain one original-row witness per boundary tuple, and store the local carriers additively rather than as a Cartesian product.
theorem.reconstruction_rule: Set C=s, use the transformed boundary assignment to select one stored original row independently for each target factor, merge the pairwise-disjoint residual assignments, and verify the full original instance.
theorem.complexity: All discovery, conditioning, residual-dependency audit, projection, portfolio storage, handoff, reconstruction and verification are polynomial in the original explicit input length; no target-factor Cartesian product is materialized and no L^2 budget is raised.
